observations: A large rounded head-like form fills the frame, split vertically by a pale olive-brown stripe on the left and a darker gray field on the right.

Two circular eye-like shapes contain concentric rings; the left one is larger with yellow-green tones and white zigzag marks at its rim, while the right sits lower and is ringed in pink and dark lines.
A tooth-filled mouth at the bottom shows a row of white block-shaped teeth outlined in red, with heavy black scribbled lines forming the jaw and surrounding area.
reading: The face-like form feels compressed—thick black outlines press the shape inward against a muted brown ground that offers little open space. Two eye-like circles, each fringed with small white fang marks, read as watchful and uneasy. A vertical color divide splits the head into mismatched halves, producing lopsided tension. The exposed teeth below widen the impression of something caught mid-howl.
contextAngle: Within the owned rawblocks subset, this work sits between "nnxyz rawblocks #53" and "nnxyz rawblocks #55" by title number. Compared to both neighbors, it uses a darker, more restrained palette—the brown ground and limited color accents contrast with the saturated blues, reds, and teals in those adjacent pieces.

connections.reason: Both share a split-face structure with asymmetric eyes, but #53 scatters bright yellow, blue, and red lines across the surface while #54 pulls color inward under heavy black strokes.
The nifty faces piece uses large radiant pink-purple eye discs that dominate its composition, whereas #54's eyes are smaller, darker, and nested in scribble—a sharp contrast in how the gaze is built.

lookingQuestion: Where do the thin colored lines—yellow, pink, light blue—appear beneath or on top of the black scribble, and how does that layering change how deep the face seems?
ambiguities: The vertical olive-brown stripe could be read as a nose divider or a color field split; the image supports either reading.
Small white zigzag marks around the eye shapes may be teeth-like motifs or decorative framing—their function is unclear.
